title: When did a stranger change your life?
author: Unknown Unknown
summary: This reflective piece explores the beauty of human connection through the concept of ichigo ichie—a Japanese phrase meaning 'one meeting, one opportunity.' The author recounts a chance encounter with a blue-eyed lady at a café who asked about the book he was reading, leading to a profound conversation where they shared personal stories without exchanging names or contact information. The article uses this moment to explore impermanence, the Japanese concepts of wabi-sabi and mono no aware, and the phenomenon of pre-emptive grief—the sadness we feel anticipating the future loss of something we have now. The piece argues that recognizing the uniqueness of each moment and letting future loss add to present joy is the key to experiencing life fully.
points: Ichigo ichie—one meeting, one opportunity—reminds us that each moment is singular and impermanent, which is what makes it precious and worthy of full presence. The beauty of talking with strangers lies in the unique magic of specific moments that will never happen again in exactly that way. Pre-emptive grief—sadness for the future loss of something you have now—is not weakness but an invitation to savor the uniqueness of the present. Recognizing that the universe has presented you with this unique moment and only you will experience it is the most special thing the universe can give. Impermanence is not something to fear or resist; it is the condition that makes any moment precious.
quotes: I recognized that the encounter will never happen again. Not like that.
One meeting, one opportunity. This is how I felt in The Smithy.
If the cherry blossoms lasted forever, nobody would travel to see them.
It's sillier to try to deny emotions. The best I can do is reframe what is going on.
